::: {#sol-default-init}

A weight $w$ drawn uniformly from $(-a, a)$ has mean 0,
so its variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Var{w}
&= \E{w^2}
&& \text{(the mean is 0)} \\
&= \int_{-a}^{a} w^2 \frac{1}{2a} \, dw
&& \text{(the density is $\frac{1}{2a}$ on $(-a, a)$)} \\
&= \frac{1}{2a} \cdot \frac{2 a^3}{3}
&& \text{(integrate $w^2$ from $-a$ to $a$)} \\
&= \frac{a^2}{3},
\end{aligned}
$$

so with $a = 1 / \sqrt{n_{\text{in}}}$ each weight has variance $1 / (3 n_{\text{in}})$.

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
_ = torch.manual_seed(0)
layer = nn.Linear(256, 256)
default_var_times_n = layer.weight.var().item() * 256
print(default_var_times_n)
```

For `nn.Linear(256, 256)` the sample variance of the weights times 256 is `r sprintf("%.3f", py$default_var_times_n)`,
close to $\frac{1}{3}$.
This variance is $\frac{1}{6}$ of [He initialization](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-he-initialization)'s $2 / n_{\text{in}}$,
so by @sol-init-scale each [ReLU](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-relu) layer with PyTorch's starting weights shrinks the values by a factor of about $1 / \sqrt{6}$.
`nn.init.kaiming_normal_` gives a layer He initialization instead.

:::
